title: Zinc plugin manifest (manifest.json)
description: The manifest at the root of a Zinc WASM plugin package (a zip with the extension .zplugin). It follows the layout of a Zotero 7 manifest.json (name, version, description, author, homepage_url, icons, applications) so a Zotero plugin author finds the same fields. Differences: `applications.zotero` is replaced by the top-level `id` and a `zinc` block; the entry is a WebAssembly component, not bootstrap.js; and permissions are declared. Version 0.1 of the plugin API; the file is design only, nothing reads it yet.

manifest_version.description: Version of this manifest format. Zotero 7 uses 2; Zinc starts at 1.

id.description: Unique plugin id. Same rules as Zotero's `applications.zotero.id`: an email-like string or a GUID in braces. It names the plugin's pref branch (`extensions.<id>.`) and its data folder, so it must never change between versions. A ported Zotero plugin keeps its id.

name.description: Display name. For a name in other languages put `name` in the locale files and use `name_l10n`.

name_l10n.description: Fluent message id (in the plugin's own .ftl files) for the display name. When the id resolves it replaces `name` in Settings > Plugins.

version.description: Semantic version, for example 1.4.0 or 2.0.0-beta.3. Zinc compares versions with the same rules as Zotero.Utilities.semverCompare. Decides ADDON_UPGRADE or ADDON_DOWNGRADE.

description_l10n.description: Fluent message id for the description.

icons.description: Icon files in the package, keyed by size in pixels, as in Zotero. SVG may be given under any key. Used in Settings > Plugins and in permission prompts.

zinc.description: What this plugin needs from Zinc. Replaces `applications.zotero` (id, strict_min_version, strict_max_version, update_url).

api_version.description: The `zinc:plugin` API version the component was built against, as MAJOR.MINOR. Zinc loads the plugin if it has the same major version and a minor version at least as high (before 1.0 the minor version must be equal, because 0.x may break between minors).

min_version.description: Lowest Zinc version. Zotero's `strict_min_version`. Below it the plugin shows as incompatible.

max_version.description: Highest Zinc version. Zotero's `strict_max_version`. Zinc does NOT enforce this unless `strict_max` is true, because Zotero's habit of pinning it (for example '7.0.*') made plugins stop on every release.

platforms.description: Operating systems the plugin works on. Default: all.

main.description: The plugin component and how it runs.

wasm.description: Path of the WebAssembly component in the package. Replaces bootstrap.js. The component targets one world of the WIT package `zinc:plugin`: `plugin` (everything), `plugin-minimal`, or one of the smaller per-family worlds (see `world` below).

world.description: Which world the component was built for.

language.description: Informational: the guest language, shown in Settings > Plugins.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the .wasm file, lower-case hex. Checked at install and at every load. If it is missing, Zinc computes it at install and pins it.

startup_timeout_ms.description: Time allowed for install, startup and shutdown hooks. Default 10000, at most 60000. Zotero has no limit; Zinc needs one because a hung plugin is stopped by killing the plugin host process.

activation_events.description: When Zinc loads the plugin. Zotero starts every enabled plugin at launch, and that is the default here (`onStartup`). A plugin that lists only the events below stays unloaded (no memory, no process time) until one happens. The plugin must declare what it contributes under `contributes` so Zinc can show placeholders and know when to wake it. Zinc then calls `startup` with reason `app-startup` (or `addon-enable`).

update_url.description: URL of the update manifest (Zotero's `applications.zotero.update_url`). Same JSON shape as Zotero's updates.json: {"addons": {"<id>": {"updates": [{"version", "update_link", "update_hash", "applications": {"zinc": {"strict_min_version"}}}]}}}. `update_link` must be https; `update_hash` (sha256:...) is required. Must be https.

optional_permissions.description: Permissions the plugin may ask for later with `permissions.request`. Not granted at install. Same shape as `permissions`; an id may not appear in both.

permission_reasons.description: Why the plugin needs a permission, shown in the install prompt and in Settings > Plugins. Keys are permission ids (or `net.hosts`); values are Fluent message ids from the plugin's .ftl files, or plain English text if the value contains a space.

default_prefs.description: Default values of the plugin's prefs, as Zotero's prefs.js `pref("extensions.<id>.key", value)` calls. Keys are relative to the plugin's own branch. Types are fixed by the default: boolean, 32-bit integer or string.

mcp.description: Tools the plugin offers to AI agents through Zinc's MCP server (plugin-api/wit/mcp.wit). Needs the permission `mcp.expose` AND the user's switch for the plugin in Settings > Plugins (off by default). The tools listed here are the static ones: they show in Settings > Plugins before the plugin runs and are served as soon as it is running. A plugin may also register tools at run time (`mcp.register-tool`). Agents see them as `<short plugin name>__<tool name>` on the HTTP endpoint of the running app only (not on the stdio transport).

locales.description: Fluent localization. Files are `<dir>/<tag>/*.ftl` in the package (Zotero: `locale/<tag>/*.ftl`).

default.description: BCP 47 tag used when no locale matches the UI language.

available.description: Tags that have a folder. If omitted, Zinc reads the folder names under `dir`.

contributes.description: Static declarations of what the plugin adds. They are hints, not a replacement for the runtime calls: they let Zinc show the entry (and wake the plugin on use) before the plugin has started, and let Settings > Plugins list what a plugin does. Entries are checked against the runtime registrations; a runtime registration with no static entry still works. Each extension area (ui, extend, reader) adds its own fields to an entry; unknown fields are allowed here and validated by that area.

reader_events.description: Reader event names the plugin listens to (see reader.wit).

uri_schemes.description: URL schemes the plugin handles, for example `zotero` sub-paths or its own.

dev.description: Development only. Ignored in a packed plugin; read when a folder is loaded in dev mode.

watch.description: Reload the plugin (shutdown with addon-upgrade, then startup) when this file changes.

packagePath.description: A relative path inside the package: '/' as separator, no '..', no leading '/'.

capability.description: A permission id, always dotted lower-case (`area.thing`, for example `reader.control`; never `annotations:read`). `examples` and `x-risk` list every id that any WIT file or report uses in 0.1 (37 ids); the host rejects ids it does not know. `net.hosts` is not an id here: hosts go under `permissions.net.hosts`. A user's pick in a file dialog or a drop is the consent for that file, so there is no id for file dialogs, and the clipboard and URL ids are the lifecycle ones only.

capabilities.description: Permission ids the plugin uses. Free capabilities need no entry: `prefs` (own branch), `l10n`, `log`, `timers`, `util`, `fs` with the roots `data`, `bundled`, `temp` and user-picked files, and all declarative UI contributions.

net.description: Network access (`net` interface and any call of another area that makes Zinc fetch a URL for the plugin).

hosts.description: Allowed hosts. Each entry is `scheme://host[:port]`, with a leading `*.` allowed in the host to match subdomains. Without a scheme, https is assumed. `http://` must be written out. Loopback and private-network hosts (a local model server, for example `http://localhost:11434`) must be listed by exact host and port. The single entry `*` means any public host and is shown to the user as a high-risk permission.

schemes.description: URL schemes other than http, https and mailto that `shell.open-url` may open, for example `obsidian`. The user is asked on first use of each.

mcpTool.description: A tool declared statically. Same fields as `mcp.tool-def` in mcp.wit, with the schemas written as JSON objects rather than JSON text.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema of the arguments; an object schema (`type` "object" or absent).

output_schema.description: JSON Schema of the result, when it is an object with a fixed shape.

destructive.description: The tool may delete or overwrite data (meaningful when read_only is false). Say false for tools that only add.

idempotent.description: Calling again with the same arguments changes nothing more.

contribution.description: One static contribution. `id` is the same id the plugin uses when it registers the thing at run time.

title_l10n.description: Fluent message id of the label or header.

title.description: Plain label, if there is no localized one.

accelerator.description: Default shortcut, in the notation of the `accelerator` type.

when.description: Where it shows, as the owning area defines (for example an extension point name from ui.wit or extend.wit).
